diagnosis.root_cause: Progressive optical attenuation on the subscriber's fibre path. RX power deteriorated from approximately -19.2 dBm to -26.45 dBm over seven days and is currently -27.1 dBm, while TX power remains stable and normal. This is isolated to ONU 14; other ONUs on EPON0/3 have normal RX levels.
evidence: The ONU is online and responding, so this is not an ONU-offline or PON-port failure.
Current RX power is -27.1 dBm, in the degraded range and close to the critical threshold of -28 dBm.
The seven-day RX series shows a sustained progressive decline from about -19.2 dBm to -26.45 dBm, far wider than the healthy +/-0.3 dBm noise floor.
Distance remains constant at 188 m, so the change is not explained by a changed fibre path or ranging distance.
TX power remains around 2.3 dBm and TX bias current remains within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range, making laser degradation unlikely.
Peer ONUs on EPON0/3 have normal RX levels, so the fault is isolated to this customer's fibre path rather than the PON port, splitter, or OLT.
The customer has 9 sessions in 24 hours and a 71-minute average duration, indicating signal-related instability and reauthentication well above the normal baseline.
The OLT, router, VLAN, RADIUS records, and ONU authentication state are healthy and consistent.
OLT population offline count is at the normal network baseline, and there is no evidence of an OLT-wide, router-wide, authentication, or provisioning fault.

remediation.action: Dispatch fibre access troubleshooting for this subscriber. Inspect and clean the ONU, patch leads, connectors, splice points, splitter leg, and drop fibre; perform OTDR and optical-power testing end to end. Repair or replace the degraded fibre component and verify RX power returns to the normal range. Continue monitoring RX power and session stability after repair.

ground_truth.root_cause: Progressive attenuation in the fibre path between the splitter and this customer's ONU, consistent with a bend, damaged connector or degrading splice on the drop.
expected_reasoning: Cached RX of -26.40 dBm sits in the degraded band (-25 to -28)
Telemetry shows RX falling from -19.2 to -26.4 dBm over six days against a +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so this is a trend and not a spot reading
Live RX of -27.10 is below the cached -26.40, so degradation is still progressing
TX power, TX bias current, supply voltage and distance are all flat, so the ONU laser and the fibre geometry are unchanged
Port neighbours on EPON0/3 read -19 to -22 dBm, so the PON port, feeder and splitter are healthy
The fault is therefore downstream of the splitter, in this customer's own fibre path
Nine sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline is a symptom of the marginal link, not an independent auth fault
Declining daily traffic is consistent with intermittent connectivity
distractors: Elevated session count invites a session_flapping_auth diagnosis
Declining traffic alone could suggest congestion
One neighbour (EPON0/3:21) is offline for unrelated reasons, at the 4.85% network baseline
